chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does the menstruating woman make up the prayer?' He said: 'No'. I said, 'Does she make up the fasting?' He said: 'Yes'. I said, 'From where is this derived?' He said: 'Indeed, the first one who analogized was Iblees.'
ai.seo_question: Why do menstruating women not have to make up missed prayers but must make up missed fasts?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the distinct jurisprudential treatment of menstruation, where missed fasting is obligatory to make up while missed prayers are not, a ruling derived from the Prophet's explicit instruction. The Imam’s attribution of this differentiation to Iblees highlights that the exemption from prayer is a specific divine dispensation (khass) rather than a result of human analogical reasoning (qiyas), preserving the unique status of Salah. This underscores the Shia view that ritual purity rules are divinely legislated rather than logically deduced from general principles of cleanliness.
